weeks.title: Your Development Environment: Shell, Editors and Reproducible Setups
weeks.summary: Is week aap terminal aur shell ko ek data engineer ki tarah use karna, `PATH` aur environment variables samajhna, virtual environments aur package managers se dependencies isolate karna, aur aisa setup banana seekhoge jo kisi doosre machine par bhi same result de.
concepts: **Shell aur terminal**: terminal sirf ek window hai; uske andar chalne wala program (bash, zsh, PowerShell) shell hai jo aapki command padhta hai, programs dhoondhta hai aur chalata hai. Data work mein shell isliye zaroori hai kyunki files move karna, scripts chalana, logs dekhna aur servers par kaam karna sab yahin se scriptable aur repeatable hota hai, GUI clicks se nahi.

**PATH lookup**: jab aap `python` likhte ho, shell `PATH` variable ki directories ko left se right check karta hai aur jo pehla executable milta hai wahi chalata hai. `which python` (ya Windows par `where python`) batata hai ki asal mein kaunsa chal raha hai. 'Galat Python chal raha hai' wali zyaadatar problems isi order se aati hain.

**Exit status**: har command khatam hokar ek number deti hai, `0` matlab success, non-zero matlab failure. `$?` last command ka status deta hai. `a && b` mein b tabhi chalta hai jab a succeed kare, `a || b` mein b tabhi jab a fail kare. Scripts aur CI pipelines isi status se decide karte hain ki aage badhna hai ya rukna hai.

**Environment variables aur export**: `X=5` sirf current shell ka variable banata hai; child process (jaise `python script.py`) use tabhi dekhta hai jab `export X=5` kiya ho. `X=5 cmd` sirf us ek command ke environment mein X daalta hai. Config (API URL, debug flag) isi raaste program tak pahunchta hai.

**Virtual environment**: `python -m venv .venv` project ke liye alag folder banata hai jismein apna `python` aur apni `site-packages` hoti hai. Activate karne se koi magic nahi hota: bas `.venv/bin` (Windows par `.venv\Scripts`) `PATH` ke shuru mein aa jaata hai, isliye `python` aur `pip` venv wale chalte hain. Isse do projects ke conflicting versions (ek ko library v1 chahiye, doosre ko v2) saath reh sakte hain.

**Package managers aur version specifiers**: `pip install -r requirements.txt` file mein likhe packages install karta hai. `==2.1.0` exact pin hai, `>=2.1,<3` range hai, aur `~=2.1.3` compatible release hai, matlab `>=2.1.3` aur `2.1.*` ke andar. Lock file (ya `pip freeze` ka output) har transitive dependency ka exact version record karta hai taaki kal ka install aaj jaisa ho.

**Reproducibility**: same code + same data + same environment + same random seed = same result. Iske liye dependencies pin karo, raw data ko read-only rakho, random seed set karo, paths ko project root ke relative rakho (hard-coded `C:\Users\...` nahi), aur README mein setup ke exact steps likho. Jo analysis sirf aapke laptop par chalta hai woh asal mein reproducible nahi hai.

**Editor aur tooling**: achha editor (koi bhi modern code editor) syntax highlighting, integrated terminal, debugger aur extensions deta hai. Formatter (code ko ek consistent style mein badalta hai) aur linter (bugs jaise unused variable ya undefined name pakadta hai) team mein style ki behas khatam karte hain. Inhe save par ya commit se pehle automatically chalana achhi aadat hai.

example.problem: Ek naye project mein aapko isolated environment banana hai, ek fixed version ki library daalni hai, aur aisa record rakhna hai ki teammate same setup bana sake. Steps aur har command ka kaam batao.
example.code:
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
which python                     # .../project/.venv/bin/python
pip install "requests==2.31.0"
pip freeze > requirements.txt
deactivate
# teammate ki machine par:
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
steps: `python -m venv .venv` project folder ke andar `.venv` banata hai jismein alag interpreter aur khaali site-packages hai.
`activate` `.venv/bin` ko `PATH` ke aage jodta hai; isliye `which python` ab venv ka path dikhata hai.
`pip install "requests==2.31.0"` library aur uski dependencies sirf venv mein install karta hai, system Python ko chhua bhi nahi.
`pip freeze > requirements.txt` har installed package ka exact `name==version` file mein likhta hai, transitive dependencies samet.
`.venv` folder ko git mein commit nahi karte (woh bada aur machine-specific hai); sirf `requirements.txt` commit hota hai.
Answer: teammate **naya venv banakar `pip install -r requirements.txt` chalata hai** aur use bilkul wahi versions milte hain.

mistakes: Venv activate kiye bina `pip install` chala dena. Package global Python mein chala jaata hai aur script venv mein 'ModuleNotFoundError' deti hai. Fix: pehle `which python`/`which pip` se check karo, ya `python -m pip install ...` use karo taaki pip usi interpreter ka ho.

`.venv` ya `__pycache__` ko git mein commit kar dena. Ye machine-specific hain aur repo ko bhaari banaate hain. Fix: inhe `.gitignore` mein daalo aur sirf `requirements.txt` (ya lock file) share karo.

Script mein relative path likh kar sochna ki woh script ki location se resolve hoga. Relative path current working directory se resolve hota hai. Fix: project root se chalao, ya Python mein `Path(__file__).parent` se path banao.
revision: `PATH` left se right search hota hai; pehla match jeetta hai.
Exit status 0 = success; `&&` success par, `||` failure par chalta hai.
`export` ke bina variable child process tak nahi pahunchta.
Venv activate = venv ki bin directory `PATH` ke aage.
Reproducible = pinned deps + fixed seed + relative paths + documented steps.

questions.question: `source .venv/bin/activate` chalane par asal mein kya badalta hai?
options: `.venv/bin` directory `PATH` ke shuru mein jud jaati hai, isliye `python` aur `pip` venv wale resolve hote hain
System Python ke saare packages `.venv` mein copy ho jaate hain
Ek naya container start hota hai jismein project chalta hai
Global `site-packages` permanently venv ki taraf point karne lagti hai
questions.explanation: Activation script mainly `PATH` ko badalti hai (aur prompt mein naam dikhati hai). Isliye `python`/`pip` likhne par venv ke executables pehle milte hain, aur woh apni alag site-packages use karte hain. Option B galat hai: venv khaali shuru hota hai, kuch copy nahi hota. Option D ka trap ye sochna hai ki activation global setting badalta hai; woh sirf current shell session tak seemit hai, `deactivate` ya naya terminal kholte hi khatam.

questions.question: `PATH` ki value `/opt/tools/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin` hai. `python` naam ka executable `/usr/local/bin` aur `/usr/bin` dono mein hai, `/opt/tools/bin` mein nahi. Terminal mein `python` likhne par kaunsa chalega?
options: `/usr/bin/python`, kyunki system directories ko priority milti hai
Shell error dega kyunki do jagah same naam hai
`/usr/local/bin/python`, kyunki `PATH` mein woh pehle aata hai
Jo version number mein naya ho, wahi
questions.explanation: Shell `PATH` ki directories left se right check karta hai aur pehla match chala deta hai. `/opt/tools/bin` mein `python` nahi hai, agla `/usr/local/bin` hai jahan mil gaya, to search wahin ruk jaata hai. Option A ka trap ye maanna hai ki `/usr/bin` 'system' hone se jeetegi; shell ke liye sirf order matter karta hai. Option D galat hai kyunki shell versions compare hi nahi karta.

questions.question: Ek directory mein `missing.txt` naam ki koi file nahi hai. Ye bash line kya print karegi?
questions.code: test -f missing.txt && echo found || echo absent; echo $?
questions.explanation: `test -f missing.txt` fail hota hai (status 1), isliye `&& echo found` skip hota hai aur `|| echo absent` chalta hai, jo 'absent' print karta hai. `$?` hamesha SABSE AAKHRI command ka status hai, aur woh `echo absent` thi jo successful rahi, to 0 print hota hai. Option A ka trap ye sochna hai ki `$?` abhi bhi `test` ka 1 yaad rakhega.

questions.question: `requirements.txt` mein `pandas~=1.5.2` likha hai (PEP 440 compatible-release operator). Inmein se kaunsa version is specifier ko satisfy karta hai?
questions.explanation: `~=1.5.2` ka matlab hai `>=1.5.2` aur `==1.5.*`, yaani last component badh sakta hai par `1.5` series se bahar nahi ja sakte. 1.5.3 dono shartein poori karta hai. 1.5.1 lower bound se neeche hai (option A). Option B ka trap `~=` ko sirf 'major version same rahe' samajhna hai; woh rule `~=1.5` (do components) ka hota, `~=1.5.2` ka nahi.

questions.question: Project layout: `/home/u/proj/data/raw.csv` aur `/home/u/proj/src/load.py`. `load.py` mein `open("data/raw.csv")` likha hai. Aap `cd /home/u/proj/src` karke `python load.py` chalate ho. Kya hoga?
options: File khul jaayegi, kyunki path script ki location se resolve hota hai
Python khud parent directories mein `data/` dhoondh lega
`PermissionError`, kyunki `src` se bahar ki file nahi padh sakte
questions.explanation: Relative path current working directory (jahan se command chalayi) ke against resolve hota hai, script ki location ke against nahi. CWD `/home/u/proj/src` hai, isliye Python `src/data/raw.csv` dhoondhta hai jo exist nahi karti. Option A sabse common galatfehmi hai. Fix: project root se `python src/load.py` chalao, ya `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "raw.csv"` jaisa path banao. Option C galat hai: Python apne aap parent folders search nahi karta.

questions.question: Ek nayi bash shell mein (jahan A, B, C pehle se set nahi hain) ye lines chalayi gayi. Output kya hoga?
questions.code:
A=1
export B=2
C=3 bash -c 'echo "A=$A B=$B C=$C"'
echo "C=$C"
questions.explanation: `bash -c` ek child process hai; usse sirf exported variables milte hain. A export nahi hua, isliye child mein khaali; B export hua, isliye 2. `C=3 cmd` C ko sirf us ek command ke environment mein daalta hai, isliye child ko C=3 milta hai par parent shell mein C kabhi set hi nahi hua, to aakhri line `C=` deti hai. Option D ka trap ye maanna hai ki har shell variable child tak pahunchta hai; option A ka trap ye ki `C=3 cmd` parent mein bhi C set kar deta hai.

weeks.title: Version Control with Git and Team Workflows
weeks.summary: Is week aap git ka internal model (working tree, staging area, commits, branches) samjhoge, merge aur conflicts handle karna, `.gitignore` likhna, mistakes ko safely undo karna aur pull request wala team workflow seekhoge.
concepts: **Teen areas**: working tree (disk par aapki files), staging area ya index (agle commit ka draft) aur repository (saved commits). `git add` file ka us waqt ka content index mein daalta hai, `git commit` index ka snapshot save karta hai. Isliye `add` ke baad file badli to woh naya badlaav commit mein nahi jaata jab tak dobara `add` na karo.

**Commit aur hash**: har commit poore project ka snapshot hai jismein author, message aur parent commit(s) ka pointer hota hai. Iska ID content se bana hash hai, isliye history badalne par hash bhi badal jaata hai. Commits ek chain (asal mein graph) banate hain jise `git log --oneline --graph` dikhata hai.

**Branch aur HEAD**: branch bas ek movable pointer hai jo kisi commit par point karta hai; naya commit karne par current branch aage khisak jaati hai. `HEAD` batata hai ki aap abhi kis branch (ya commit) par ho. `git switch -c feature` naya pointer banata hai, files copy nahi karta, isliye branch banana sasta hai.

**Merge ke do roop**: agar `main` branch banne ke baad aage nahi badhi, to `git merge feature` sirf pointer aage kar deta hai (fast-forward, koi naya commit nahi). Agar dono taraf naye commits hain, to git common ancestor se teen-tarfa (three-way) merge karke ek **merge commit** banata hai jiske do parents hote hain.

**Conflicts**: jab dono branches ne same file ki same lines alag tarah badli hon, git khud decide nahi karta aur file mein markers daal deta hai: `<<<<<<< HEAD` ke neeche aapki current branch ka version, `=======` ke baad merge ho rahi branch ka version, aur `>>>>>>> feature` par end. Aap sahi content rakhte ho, markers hataate ho, phir `git add` aur `git commit`.

**Remotes**: `origin` ek remote repository ka naam hai. `git fetch` remote ke naye commits download karke `origin/main` jaise remote-tracking branches update karta hai, par aapki local branch aur files ko nahi chhoota. `git pull` = fetch + merge (ya rebase) current branch mein. `git push` aapke commits remote par bhejta hai.

**.gitignore**: patterns jo untracked files ko `git status` aur `git add .` se chhupaate hain: `*.csv` har level par, `/build` sirf repo root ka build, `logs/` kisi bhi level ki logs directory, aur `!data/keep.csv` exception. Ye sirf untracked files par lagta hai; jo file pehle se tracked hai use `git rm --cached` se untrack karna padta hai.

**Undo aur PR workflow**: `git restore file` working tree ke badlaav hataata hai, `git restore --staged file` file ko unstage karta hai, `git revert <hash>` ek naya commit banata hai jo purane commit ka ulta karta hai (shared history safe rehti hai), jabki `git reset` branch pointer peeche le jaata hai (history rewrite). Team mein kaam feature branch par hota hai, push karke pull request kholte ho, review aur CI pass hone ke baad merge hota hai.

example.problem: Aap `main` par ho. Ek `feature` branch mein `config.py` ki line `rate = 0.07` ki gayi, aur isi beech `main` par wahi line `rate = 0.05` ki gayi. `git merge feature` chalane ke baad conflict ko kaise resolve karoge?
example.code:
git merge feature
# CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in config.py
cat config.py
<<<<<<< HEAD
rate = 0.05
=======
rate = 0.07
>>>>>>> feature
# file edit karke sirf sahi line rakho, phir:
git add config.py
git commit
steps: Dono branches ne common ancestor ke baad same line badli, isliye git automatic merge nahi kar sakta.
`<<<<<<< HEAD` aur `=======` ke beech `main` (current branch) ka version hai: `rate = 0.05`.
`=======` aur `>>>>>>> feature` ke beech merge ho rahi branch ka version hai: `rate = 0.07`.
Team se poochh kar sahi value decide karo (maan lo 0.07), aur teeno marker lines delete karo.
`git add config.py` git ko batata hai ki conflict resolve ho gaya; `git commit` merge commit banata hai jiske do parents hain.
Answer: **file mein sirf `rate = 0.07` rakho, markers hatao, `git add` + `git commit`**.

mistakes: Pehle se tracked file (jaise `secrets.env`) ko `.gitignore` mein daal kar sochna ki ab git use ignore karega. Tracked files par ignore rules nahi lagte. Fix: `git rm --cached secrets.env`, commit karo, aur agar secret push ho chuka tha to use rotate karo (history mein woh abhi bhi hai).

Shared branch par `git reset --hard` karke force-push kar dena. Teammates ki history aur aapki history alag ho jaati hai aur unka kaam toot sakta hai. Fix: published commits ko `git revert` se undo karo.

Conflict resolve karte waqt `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>` markers file mein chhod dena. Code syntax error dega ya data file kharab hogi. Fix: commit se pehle `git diff --check` ya file search karke markers dhoondho.
revision: `git add` us pal ka content stage karta hai; baad ke edits ke liye dobara add.
Branch = commit par movable pointer; HEAD = aap kahan ho.
Fast-forward mein naya commit nahi; three-way merge mein do parents wala merge commit.
`fetch` sirf download, `pull` = fetch + merge.
`.gitignore` sirf untracked files par; tracked ke liye `git rm --cached`.
Shared history ke liye `revert`, `reset` nahi.

questions.question: Teammate ne remote `main` par 3 naye commits push kiye. Aap apni local `main` par `git fetch origin` chalate ho. Iske turant baad kya sach hai?
options: Aapki local `main` aur working tree mein teeno commits aa gaye
Git ne automatically ek merge commit bana diya
Kuch download nahi hua; uske liye `git pull` chahiye
Naye commits `origin/main` mein aa gaye, par local `main` aur aapki files wahi ki wahi hain
questions.explanation: `git fetch` sirf remote se objects download karke remote-tracking branch `origin/main` ko update karta hai. Aapki local branch tab badlegi jab aap `git merge origin/main` karoge (ya `git pull`, jo fetch + merge hai). Option A ka trap fetch ko pull samajhna hai. Option C ulta galat hai: download fetch hi karta hai, pull bas uske upar merge jodta hai.

questions.question: Aap `main` par ho aur `git merge feature` ke baad `report.py` mein ye conflict aaya. `main` branch ka version kaunsa hai?
questions.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD
threshold = 0.8
=======
threshold = 0.75
>>>>>>> feature
options: Dono lines `feature` branch se aayi hain
Markers se pata nahi chalta; `git log` dekhna padega
questions.explanation: `<<<<<<< HEAD` se `=======` tak ka hissa HEAD, yaani current checked-out branch ka hai. Aap `main` par ho, isliye `threshold = 0.8` main ka version hai, aur `=======` se `>>>>>>> feature` tak wala (0.75) merge ho rahi `feature` branch ka. Option B ka trap HEAD ko 'nayi aane wali' branch samajhna hai.

questions.question: `a.txt` tracked hai aur committed content `v1` hai. Ye commands chalayi gayi. Naye commit mein `a.txt` ka content kya hoga, aur `git status` kya dikhayega?
questions.code:
echo v2 > a.txt
git add a.txt
echo v3 > a.txt
git commit -m "update"
options: Commit mein `v1`; kyunki commit se pehle file dobara badal gayi
Commit fail hoga kyunki staged aur working version alag hain
questions.explanation: `git add` us waqt ka content (`v2`) index mein snapshot kar leta hai. Uske baad `v3` likhna sirf working tree badalta hai. `git commit` index se commit banata hai, isliye commit mein `v2` jaata hai, aur `v3` ek unstaged modification ke roop mein bacha rehta hai. Option A ka trap ye maanna hai ki `add` file ka 'naam' track karta hai aur commit latest content le leta hai.

questions.question: `main` par commits C1, C2 hain. `feature` branch C2 se bani aur usmein C3, C4, C5 commit hue. Isi beech `main` par C6 commit hua. Ab `main` par `git merge feature` chalaya (koi conflict nahi). `git rev-list --count main` kya dega?
questions.explanation: Dono branches C2 ke baad alag-alag aage badhi hain, isliye fast-forward possible nahi; git three-way merge karke ek naya merge commit banata hai jiske do parents (C6 aur C5) hain. `main` se reachable commits: C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 aur merge commit = 7. Option B ka trap merge commit ko bhool jaana hai, jo fast-forward wale case mein sahi hota.

questions.question: Ek buggy commit `a1b2c3d` pehle hi shared `main` par push ho chuka hai aur teammates ne uske upar kaam pull kar liya hai. Iska effect hatane ka sabse safe tareeka kaunsa hai?
options: `git revert a1b2c3d` karke naya commit push karna
`.gitignore` mein badli hui files daal dena
Local repo delete karke dobara clone karna
questions.explanation: `git revert` ek naya commit banata hai jo us commit ke changes ko ulta karta hai; purani history nahi badalti, isliye teammates normal pull kar sakte hain. Option B local history mein se commit hata deta hai aur force-push shared history rewrite karta hai, jisse teammates ke branches diverge ho jaate hain. Ye sabse tempting trap hai kyunki apni machine par 'saaf' dikhta hai. Option C ka tracked files par koi asar nahi.

questions.question: Repo root par ye `.gitignore` hai. Inmein se kaunsi untracked file `git status` mein dikhegi (yaani ignore NAHI hogi)?
questions.code:
*.csv
!data/keep.csv
/build
logs/
questions.explanation: `/build` ke shuru mein slash hai, isliye ye sirf repo root wali `build` ko match karta hai; `src/build/` match nahi hota, to `src/build/main.o` dikhegi. `data/raw.csv` ko `*.csv` ignore karta hai (exception sirf `keep.csv` ke liye hai). `build/main.o` root ki build mein hai, ignored. `logs/` bina leading slash ke kisi bhi level ki `logs` directory match karta hai, isliye `app/logs/run.txt` bhi ignored. Option D ka trap ye sochna hai ki `logs/` sirf root par lagta hai.

weeks.title: HTTP APIs, JSON and Serving a Small Python App
weeks.summary: Is week aap HTTP request-response ka poora structure, status codes aur methods ke semantics, JSON ke exact rules, ek chhoti Python web API kaise serve hoti hai, aur config/secrets ko environment variables se kaise sambhalte hain, ye seekhoge.
concepts: **HTTP request ka structure**: method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), URL, headers aur optional body. URL ke hisse: scheme (`https`), host (`api.example.com`), port (`:8443`, na likho to https ke liye 443), path (`/v1/items`), query string (`?page=2&tag=x`) aur fragment (`#top`, jo browser mein hi rehta hai, server tak nahi jaata). Response mein status code, headers (jaise `Content-Type: application/json`) aur body aati hai.

**Status code families**: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content), 3xx redirect (301 permanent, 302/307 temporary), 4xx client ki galti (400 bad request, 401 authentication missing/invalid, 403 authenticated par permission nahi, 404 not found, 405 method not allowed, 429 too many requests), 5xx server ki galti (500 internal error, 503 unavailable). Retry ka faisla isi par hota hai: 4xx par wahi request dobara bhejna aksar bekaar hai (429 apvaad hai), 5xx/429 par backoff ke saath retry samajhdaari hai.

**Methods ke semantics**: GET safe hai (server state nahi badalta) aur idempotent. PUT (poora resource replace) aur DELETE idempotent hain: ek baar bhejo ya paanch baar, final state same. POST idempotent nahi: do baar bhejne par do orders ban sakte hain. Isliye network timeout ke baad POST ko blindly retry nahi karte; idempotency key jaisa mechanism chahiye.

**REST style**: URLs resources (nouns) ko naam dete hain, actions methods se aate hain: `GET /users/42`, `POST /users`, `DELETE /users/42`. Filtering, sorting, paging query parameters se: `GET /orders?status=paid&page=3`. Response mein consistent JSON shape aur sahi status code dena client ka kaam aasaan karta hai.

**JSON ke rules**: types sirf object, array, string, number, `true`/`false` aur `null` hain. Keys aur strings double quotes mein hi, trailing comma aur comments allowed nahi, `undefined`/`NaN` valid JSON nahi. Python mein `json.dumps` dict ko JSON banata hai: tuple array ban jaata hai, `None` `null` aur `True` `true`; non-string keys (jaise 1) string `"1"` ban jaati hain. Isliye round-trip ke baad object hamesha pehle jaisa nahi milta.

**Python app serve karna**: ek web framework route (method + path) ko function se map karta hai; function request padhta hai aur response (JSON + status) lautata hai. Server ek host aur port par listen karta hai: `127.0.0.1` matlab sirf isi machine se connection, `0.0.0.0` matlab saare network interfaces se. Development server debugging ke liye hai; production mein proper application server aur reverse proxy lagaye jaate hain.

**Environment variables aur secrets**: config jo deployment ke saath badalta hai (database URL, API keys, port) code mein nahi, environment mein rakho, aur `os.environ` se padho. `os.environ` ki har value string hoti hai, isliye number chahiye to `int(...)` karo. Local development mein `.env` file use hoti hai jo `.gitignore` mein hoti hai; repo mein sirf `.env.example` jaati hai jismein dummy values hon.

**API keys ki safety**: key ko URL query mein bhejna risky hai kyunki URLs server logs, browser history aur proxies mein record hote hain; header (jaise `Authorization: Bearer <token>`) behtar hai. Key leak ho jaaye to sirf commit delete karna kaafi nahi, key ko revoke/rotate karo.

example.problem: Ek chhota prediction API chahiye: `POST /predict` JSON body `{"area": 1200}` le, aur JSON mein price lautaye. Model ka version environment se aaye. Code aur ek sample request-response samjhao.
example.code:
import os
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)
MODEL_VERSION = os.environ.get("MODEL_VERSION", "dev")

@app.post("/predict")
def predict():
    body = request.get_json(silent=True)
    if not body or "area" not in body:
        return jsonify(error="area is required"), 400
    price = 5000 * float(body["area"])
    return jsonify(price=price, model=MODEL_VERSION), 200

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")))

# curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/predict \
#      -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"area": 1200}'
steps: `@app.post("/predict")` route ko function se jodta hai: sirf POST method aur `/predict` path par ye chalega; GET bhejoge to 405 aayega.
`request.get_json(silent=True)` body ko JSON ki tarah parse karta hai; invalid ya missing body par `None` milta hai.
Agar `area` missing hai to client ki galti hai, isliye 400 aur ek clear error message lautaate hain, 500 nahi.
Valid input par price = 5000 × 1200 = 6000000.0 calculate hota hai aur `jsonify` use JSON response banata hai.
`MODEL_VERSION` aur `PORT` environment se aate hain; `PORT` string hai, isliye `int(...)` kiya.
Answer: response **status 200**, aur JSON body mein `price` = 6000000.0 aur `model` = "dev" (agar `MODEL_VERSION` set nahi hai).

mistakes: Har error par 200 bhej kar body mein `"error"` likh dena. Client, monitoring aur retry logic status code dekhte hain. Fix: validation fail par 400/422, auth par 401/403, missing resource par 404, aur sirf genuinely server failure par 5xx.

API key ko code mein hard-code karke repo push kar dena. Git history se woh kabhi asaani se nahi jaati. Fix: key environment variable se padho, `.env` ko ignore karo, aur leak hui key turant rotate karo.
`os.environ["PORT"]` ko number samajh kar maths karna. Environment values hamesha strings hain, isliye `"8000" + "1"` `"80001"` banta hai. Fix: `int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000"))`.
revision: 4xx = client ki galti, 5xx = server ki galti; 401 = kaun ho pata nahi, 403 = pata hai par ijaazat nahi.
GET, PUT, DELETE idempotent; POST nahi.
JSON: double quotes, no trailing comma, no comments, `null` not `None`.
`json.dumps` mein tuple → array aur int key → string key.
`127.0.0.1` sirf local; `0.0.0.0` saare interfaces.
Secrets environment mein, `.env` gitignored, values strings.

questions.question: Client valid token bhejta hai (server ne user pehchaan liya), par us user ko `/admin/reports` dekhne ki permission nahi hai. Sabse sahi status code kaunsa hai?
questions.explanation: User authenticate ho chuka hai, problem sirf authorization (permission) ki hai, jiske liye 403 hai. 401 tab hota hai jab credentials missing ya invalid hon, yaani server ko pata hi nahi aap kaun ho; naam 'Unauthorized' hone ki wajah se option A sabse tempting trap hai. 500 server ki khud ki galti ke liye hai, yahan server sahi kaam kar raha hai.

questions.question: Inmein se kaunsa string valid JSON hai (Python ka `json.loads` bina error ke parse karega)?
questions.explanation: JSON mein keys/strings double quotes mein, `null` allowed, numbers integer ya decimal dono ho sakte hain, isliye option D valid hai. Option A Python dict jaisa dikhta hai par single quotes JSON mein invalid hain; ye sabse common trap hai jab log `str(dict)` ko JSON samajh lete hain. Option B mein trailing comma hai, aur option C mein `undefined` JavaScript ka concept hai, JSON ka nahi.

questions.question: Is Python code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import json
d = {1: (2, 3), "x": None, "y": True}
s = json.dumps(d)
back = json.loads(s)
print(s)
print(back == d)
options: `TypeError`, kyunki tuple JSON mein convert nahi hota
questions.explanation: `json.dumps` int key 1 ko string `"1"`, tuple ko array, `None` ko `null` aur `True` ko `true` banata hai. Wapas `loads` karne par key `"1"` (string) aur value list `[2, 3]` milti hai, jabki original mein key int 1 aur value tuple thi, isliye `back == d` False hai. Option B ka trap ye maanna hai ki JSON round-trip lossless hai. Option D galat hai: tuple serialize hota hai, bas list ban kar.

questions.question: Network timeout ki wajah se client ko pata nahi ki request server tak pahunchi ya nahi. HTTP semantics ke hisaab se kin methods ko bina side-effect ki chinta ke dobara bhejna safe hai, kyunki ve idempotent hain?
options: Saare methods, kyunki server duplicate pehchaan leta hai
questions.explanation: Idempotent ka matlab hai ek baar ya kai baar bhejne par server ki final state same rahe. GET (safe), PUT (resource ko same value se replace) aur DELETE (doosri baar bhi resource gayab hi rehta hai, chahe response 404 aaye) idempotent hain. POST nahi hai: do baar bhejne se do records ban sakte hain, isliye option C galat hai. Option A ka trap 'safe' aur 'idempotent' ko ek samajhna hai; PUT/DELETE safe nahi par idempotent hain.

questions.question: Is Python code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import os
os.environ["PORT"] = "8000"
os.environ.pop("API_KEY", None)
print(os.environ.get("API_KEY"), os.environ["PORT"] + "1")
options: `"" 80001` (missing variable khaali string deta hai, jaise shell mein)
questions.explanation: `pop("API_KEY", None)` key ko hata deta hai (na ho to bhi error nahi). `os.environ.get("API_KEY")` missing key par `None` lautata hai, `KeyError` sirf `os.environ["API_KEY"]` jaise square-bracket access par aata (option A ka trap). Environment values strings hain, isliye `"8000" + "1"` string concatenation se `"80001"` banta hai. Option B ka trap PORT ko integer maan kar 8001 jodna hai.

questions.question: Is Python code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
from urllib.parse import urlsplit, parse_qs
u = urlsplit("https://api.example.com:8443/v1/items?tag=data%20science&page=2&page=3#top")
q = parse_qs(u.query)
print(u.port, u.path, q["tag"][0], q["page"])
questions.explanation: URL mein port explicitly 8443 diya hai, path query string ke bina `/v1/items` hai, aur fragment `#top` query mein nahi aata. `parse_qs` percent-encoding decode karta hai (`%20` → space) aur har key ki values ki LIST deta hai; `page` do baar aaya hai to `['2', '3']`. Option C ka trap dict ki tarah 'aakhri value jeetti hai' sochna hai, option A ka trap ye ki decoding nahi hoti. Option D https ka default port maan leta hai jabki port URL mein likha hai.

weeks.title: Containers, Hosting Models and Continuous Integration
weeks.summary: Is week aap image aur container ka fark, Dockerfile ke instructions aur layer caching, port mapping, static hosting aur serverless ka idea, aur har push par tests chalane wali CI pipeline ki basics seekhoge.
concepts: **Container kyun**: 'mere laptop par to chal raha tha' ki problem isliye aati hai kyunki OS libraries, Python version aur packages har machine par alag hote hain. Container app ko uski poori runtime (OS userland, interpreter, libraries) ke saath pack karta hai, par host ka kernel share karta hai, isliye virtual machine se bahut halka aur jaldi start hone wala hota hai.

**Image vs container**: image ek read-only template hai (layers ka stack), container us image ka chalta hua (ya ruka hua) instance hai jiske upar ek patli writable layer hoti hai. Ek image se kai containers ban sakte hain, jaise ek class se kai objects. Container delete karte hi uski writable layer ka data chala jaata hai; jo data bachana hai woh volume ya bahar ke storage mein rakho.

**Dockerfile instructions**: `FROM` base image chunta hai, `WORKDIR` working directory set karta hai, `COPY` files image mein daalta hai, `RUN` BUILD ke waqt command chalata hai (jaise `pip install`) aur nayi layer banata hai, `ENV` environment variable set karta hai, `EXPOSE` sirf document karta hai ki app kaunsa port use karta hai, aur `CMD` container START hone par chalne wali default command hai. Kai `CMD` likhe hon to sirf aakhri wala maana jaata hai, aur `docker run image <cmd>` use override kar deta hai.

**Layer caching**: har instruction ek layer hai; rebuild mein Docker tab tak cache use karta hai jab tak instruction aur uske inputs nahi badle. Pehla badla hua step aur uske baad ke saare steps dobara chalte hain. Isliye pehle sirf `requirements.txt` copy karke `pip install` karo, phir baaki code copy karo; code badalne par dependencies dobara install nahi hongi.

**Ports aur networking**: container ka apna network namespace hota hai. `docker run -p 8080:5000 img` ka matlab host ka port 8080 container ke port 5000 par forward hoga (format `HOST:CONTAINER`). Container ke andar app ko `0.0.0.0` par listen karna chahiye; `127.0.0.1` par listen karega to woh sirf container ke andar se reachable hoga aur forwarded traffic tak nahi pahunchega.

**Static hosting**: agar site sirf HTML, CSS, JavaScript aur data files hai (koi server-side code nahi), to use static host par serve kar sakte ho: server files ko jaise hain waise bhej deta hai, sasta, tez aur CDN-friendly. Dashboard ya report jo browser mein hi JSON padh kar chart banata hai, static ho sakta hai; Python API jo request par calculation karta hai, static nahi ho sakta.

**Serverless**: aap sirf ek function deploy karte ho, platform request aane par use chalata hai aur load ke hisaab se scale karta hai. Function stateless hona chahiye: do requests ke beech memory ya local disk par bharosa mat karo, state database/object storage mein rakho. Kaafi der idle rehne ke baad pehli request 'cold start' ki wajah se dheemi ho sakti hai, aur execution time ki limits hoti hain.

**CI (continuous integration)**: har push ya pull request par ek automated pipeline saaf machine par code checkout karti hai, dependencies install karti hai, linter aur tests chalati hai, aur fail hone par merge rokti hai. Pipeline ek YAML file mein steps ki tarah likhi jaati hai; koi step non-zero exit status de to job fail. Secrets (deploy tokens) CI ke secret store mein rakhe jaate hain, repo mein nahi.

example.problem: Ek chhoti Python API (`app.py`, port 5000) ko container mein pack karna hai aur host par `http://localhost:8080` se kholna hai. Dockerfile aur commands likho, aur batao ki code badalne par rebuild fast kyun rahega.
example.code:
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
ENV PORT=5000
EXPOSE 5000
CMD ["python", "app.py"]

# app.py ke andar: app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000)

docker build -t price-api:1 .
docker run --rm -p 8080:5000 price-api:1
steps: `FROM` ek chhota Python base image leta hai; `WORKDIR /app` aage ke saare paths ka base banata hai.
Pehle sirf `requirements.txt` copy hoti hai aur `RUN pip install` chalta hai; ye layer tab tak cached rahegi jab tak requirements file nahi badalti.
`COPY . .` baaki code daalta hai; `app.py` badalne par sirf yahin se aage ke steps dobara bante hain.
`CMD` build ke waqt nahi chalta, container start hone par chalta hai.
App `0.0.0.0` par listen karta hai taaki container ke network interface par aane wala forwarded traffic use mile.
`-p 8080:5000` host port 8080 ko container port 5000 se jodta hai; `--rm` container rukte hi use delete kar deta hai.
Answer: **browser mein `http://localhost:8080` kholo**; code change par sirf `COPY . .` se aage ki layers rebuild hongi, `pip install` cache se aayega.

mistakes: Container ke andar data (jaise SQLite file ya uploads) likh kar sochna ki woh hamesha rahega. Container hatate hi writable layer chali jaati hai. Fix: volume mount karo ya bahar ke database/object storage mein likho.

`COPY . .` ko `pip install` se pehle rakhna. Har chhote code change par poori dependencies dobara install hoti hain aur build bahut dheema ho jaata hai. Fix: pehle requirements copy + install, phir code copy.
`EXPOSE 5000` likh kar sochna ki port host par khul gaya. `EXPOSE` sirf documentation hai. Fix: `docker run -p HOST:CONTAINER` se publish karo.
revision: Image = read-only template; container = uska running/stopped instance + writable layer.
`RUN` build time par, `CMD` container start par; aakhri `CMD` hi gine jaata hai.
Pehla badla step aur uske baad sab rebuild; dependencies pehle install karo.
`-p HOST:CONTAINER`; container ke andar `0.0.0.0` par bind karo.
Static hosting = sirf files; serverless = stateless function + cold start.
CI har push par install + lint + test; non-zero exit = fail.

questions.question: Machine par pehle koi container nahi tha. Aapne ek image `etl:1` build ki aur `docker run etl:1` teen baar chalaya (bina `--rm` ke). Har baar script khatam hokar container exit ho gaya. Ab `docker ps -a` kitne containers dikhayega, aur `etl` ki kitni images hongi?
questions.explanation: Har `docker run` usi ek image se ek naya container banata hai, isliye 3 containers aur 1 image. Exit hone ke baad bhi container stopped state mein rehta hai jab tak `--rm` na diya ho ya `docker rm` na kiya ho, aur `docker ps -a` stopped containers bhi dikhata hai. Option D ka trap 'exit = delete' maanna hai; option C ka trap har run par nayi image banne ki galatfehmi hai.

questions.question: Container ke andar API port 5000 par `0.0.0.0` pe listen kar rahi hai. Aap `docker run -p 8080:5000 myapi` chalate ho. Host machine ke browser se API kis URL par milegi?
questions.explanation: `-p` ka format `HOST:CONTAINER` hai: host ka 8080 container ke 5000 par forward hota hai, isliye host se `localhost:8080` kholte hain. Option A ka trap order ulta padhna hai (container port ko host port samajhna); host par 5000 publish hi nahi hua. Option B mein container ke andar to 5000 hai, 8080 nahi.

questions.question: Is Dockerfile se image banayi aur `docker run img` (bina extra arguments) chalaya. Container start hone par kaunsi command chalegi?
questions.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN python setup_data.py
CMD ["python", "train.py"]
CMD ["python", "serve.py"]
questions.explanation: Dockerfile mein sirf aakhri `CMD` effective hota hai, isliye container start par `python serve.py` chalta hai. `RUN python setup_data.py` image BUILD ke waqt ek baar chal chuka hai, har container start par nahi, isliye option D galat hai. Option C ka trap ye sochna hai ki kai `CMD` script ki tarah order mein chalte hain.

questions.question: Ek team apni image-resize service ko serverless function ke roop mein deploy kar rahi hai. Inmein se kaunsa statement sahi design guidance hai?
options: Function ke global variable mein counter rakho; woh har request ke beech guaranteed bacha rahega
Serverless ka matlab hai koi server hota hi nahi, isliye latency hamesha zero hai
Function ko stateless likho, state database/object storage mein rakho, aur idle ke baad pehli request mein cold-start delay ki ummeed rakho
Function ko khud ek fixed port par HTTP server start karke listen karna padta hai
questions.explanation: Serverless platform function instances ko zaroorat ke hisaab se banata aur hataata hai, isliye memory ya local disk ki state par bharosa nahi kiya ja sakta; idle ke baad naya instance banne mein cold start lagta hai. Option A sabse tempting trap hai kyunki kabhi-kabhi warm instance par value bachi dikh jaati hai, par guarantee nahi hai aur parallel instances ke apne alag counters hote hain. Option B galat hai: servers hote hain, bas platform sambhalta hai. Option D container-style soch hai; serverless mein platform hi request function tak pahunchata hai.

questions.question: Ek Flask app container mein `app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=5000)` se chalti hai. `docker run -p 5000:5000 img` ke baad host par `curl http://localhost:5000` connection error deta hai, jabki container ke andar se `curl` chal jaata hai. Sabse sahi wajah aur fix kya hai?
options: `EXPOSE 5000` missing hai; Dockerfile mein jodne se theek ho jaayega
Host par port 5000 kisi aur ne le rakha hai; `-p 5001:5000` karo
App container ke loopback par hi sun rahi hai, forwarded traffic container ke network interface par aata hai; app ko `host="0.0.0.0"` par chalao
Flask containers mein kaam nahi karta; serverless use karo
questions.explanation: Container ka `127.0.0.1` sirf container ke andar ka loopback hai. Port forwarding traffic ko container ke network interface (eth0) par bhejta hai, jahan app sun hi nahi rahi, isliye andar se curl chalta hai par bahar se nahi. `0.0.0.0` par bind karne se app saare interfaces par sunti hai. Option A tempting hai par `EXPOSE` sirf documentation hai, publishing `-p` ne pehle hi kar di. Option B mein port conflict hota to `docker run` khud start par error deta.

questions.question: Is Dockerfile se ek baar image build ho chuki hai. Ab aap sirf `app.py` badalte ho (`requirements.txt` same hai) aur dobara `docker build` chalate ho. Kaunse steps asal mein dobara execute honge?
questions.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["python", "app.py"]
options: `FROM` se `RUN pip install` tak cache se aayenge; `COPY . .` aur uske baad ke steps dobara banenge
Saare steps dobara, kyunki build context badal gaya hai
Sirf `RUN pip install` dobara chalega, kyunki woh code par depend karta hai
Kuch bhi dobara nahi; Docker purani image hi lautayega
questions.explanation: Docker har step ko cache se tab tak reuse karta hai jab tak instruction aur uske inputs same hain. `COPY requirements.txt .` ka input (requirements file) nahi badla, isliye woh aur `pip install` cached hain. `COPY . .` ka input (jismein `app.py` hai) badla, to wahi pehla invalidated step hai aur uske baad ke steps dobara bante hain. Option B ka trap ye maanna hai ki koi bhi file badalne par poora build dobara hota hai; ye tab sach hota jab `COPY . .` `pip install` se pehle hota. Option D galat hai kyunki badla hua code naye layer mein aana hi chahiye.

weeks.title: LLMs as Tools: Tokens, Context and Prompt Design
weeks.summary: Is week aap samjhoge ki large language model asal mein kya karta hai, tokens aur context window ka budget kaise banta hai, temperature kya badalta hai, aur clear instructions, examples aur structured output se aise prompts kaise likhte hain jinka output code mein bharose se use ho sake.
concepts: **LLM kya karta hai**: language model diye gaye text ke baad agla token kya hona chahiye, iski probability distribution nikaalta hai, ek token chunta hai, use input mein jodta hai aur dohraata hai. Isliye output fluent hota hai par 'sach' hone ki guarantee nahi; model facts lookup nahi karta, patterns se generate karta hai. Data work mein ise classification, extraction, summarisation, code drafting jaise tasks ke liye ek tool ki tarah use karte hain, aur output ko verify karte hain.

**Tokens**: model text ko words nahi, tokens (aksar sub-word pieces) mein todta hai. Ek lamba ya kam common word kai tokens ka ho sakta hai, aur alag languages/scripts mein same baat ke tokens bahut alag ho sakte hain. Limits, latency aur billing sab tokens mein gine jaate hain, isliye prompt chhota aur saaf rakhna seedha cost bachata hai.

**Context window**: ek request mein model jitne tokens dekh sakta hai uski limit, aur ismein input (system instructions, conversation history, documents) aur generate hone wala output DONO aate hain. Chat API stateless hoti hai: model pichhli call yaad nahi rakhta, aapka app har baar zaroori history dobara bhejta hai, isliye lambi conversation mein history ko trim ya summarise karna padta hai.

**Sampling aur temperature**: temperature kam (0 ke paas) hone par model sabse probable tokens chunta hai aur output zyada consistent hota hai; zyada temperature variety badhata hai. Extraction, classification aur code ke liye kam temperature, brainstorming ke liye zyada. Phir bhi kam temperature 'sahi' answer ki guarantee nahi, sirf consistency badhata hai.

**Prompt design ke principles**: (1) role aur task saaf likho; (2) input data ko delimiters (jaise triple quotes ya XML-style tags) mein rakho taaki instructions aur data alag dikhen; (3) output format exactly batao; (4) kuch examples do (few-shot), jo edge cases bhi cover karein; (5) zaroori ho to model ko pehle reasoning ya steps likhne do, phir final answer ek fixed field mein; (6) batao ki jaankari na mile to kya lautana hai (jaise `null` ya 'unknown').

**Structured output**: jab output code mein jaana hai, plain text ki jagah JSON maango aur ek schema (fields, types, allowed values) define karo. Response ko `json.loads` se parse karo aur validate karo: field missing, galat type (jaise age `"29"` string) ya extra text par retry ya fallback. Model ke output ko kabhi bina validation ke database ya shell command mein mat daalo.

**Tool/function calling aur injection**: kai APIs mein aap functions ka schema dete ho aur model batata hai ki kaunsa function kin arguments se call karna hai; asal call aapka code karta hai, jo arguments validate kar sakta hai. Jo text user ya documents se aata hai woh instructions jaisa dikh sakta hai ('pichhle instructions ignore karo'); isse prompt injection kehte hain. Untrusted text ko data ki tarah delimit karo aur model ko aisi permissions mat do jo galat instruction par nuksaan kar sakein.

example.problem: Customer reviews ko `positive`, `negative` ya `neutral` mein classify karna hai, aur result JSON mein chahiye taaki pipeline seedha parse kare. Ek robust prompt aur parsing logic banao.
example.code:
import json

SYSTEM = ("You classify product reviews. Reply with JSON only: "
          '{"label": "positive" | "negative" | "neutral", "reason": "<10 words>"}')

EXAMPLES = [
    ("Battery lasts two days, love it", '{"label": "positive", "reason": "praises battery life"}'),
    ("Arrived on time.", '{"label": "neutral", "reason": "states a fact only"}'),
]

def build_messages(review):
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}]
    for text, out in EXAMPLES:
        msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": f"<review>{text}</review>"})
        msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": out})
    msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": f"<review>{review}</review>"})
    return msgs

def parse(reply):
    data = json.loads(reply)
    if data.get("label") not in {"positive", "negative", "neutral"}:
        raise ValueError("bad label")
    return data
steps: System message role aur EXACT output format batata hai: sirf JSON, teen allowed labels.
Do few-shot examples dikhate hain ki format kaisa ho, aur ek neutral edge case bhi cover karte hain.
Review text `<review>` tags mein hai, taaki review ke andar likha koi 'instruction' data hi maana jaaye.
Har review ek alag stateless request hai; examples har baar dobara bheje jaate hain kyunki model kuch yaad nahi rakhta.
Temperature kam rakhte hain taaki same review par label baar-baar na badle.
`parse` JSON load karta hai aur label ko allowed set se check karta hai; fail par retry ya manual review queue.
Answer: **clear format + few-shot + delimiters + validation** wala ye pipeline free-text output se kahin zyada reliable hai.

mistakes: Model ke output ko seedha trust kar lena kyunki woh confident lagta hai. LLM galat facts ya galat format bhi utne hi confidence se de sakta hai. Fix: format ko schema se validate karo aur facts ko source data se cross-check karo.
Ye maan lena ki model pichhli API call yaad rakhega. API stateless hai, isliye doosri call mein context gayab hota hai. Fix: zaroori history (ya uska summary) har request mein bhejo.
Prompt mein sirf 'short answer do' likhna aur phir parsing fail hone par hairaan hona. Ambiguous instruction ambiguous output deta hai. Fix: exact format, allowed values aur ek-do examples do.
revision: LLM agla token predict karta hai; fluent hai, guaranteed sahi nahi.
Context window = input + output tokens; API stateless.
Kam temperature = zyada consistent, zaroori nahi ki sahi.
Prompt: role, task, delimiters, exact format, examples, fallback.
Structured output ko parse + validate karo, phir use karo.
Untrusted text ko data ki tarah delimit karo; prompt injection se bacho.

questions.question: Ek chat API ki pehli call mein user ne likha 'Mera naam Ravi hai'. Doosri, alag API call mein aap sirf `{"role": "user", "content": "Mera naam kya hai?"}` bhejte ho. Kya hoga?
options: Model 'Ravi' bolega, kyunki model har user ki conversation server par yaad rakhta hai
Model 'Ravi' bolega, kyunki pehli call se model ke weights update ho gaye
Model ko naam pata nahi hoga; use jaanne ke liye pichhle messages isi request mein bhejne padenge
API error dega kyunki pehla message missing hai
questions.explanation: Chat completion APIs stateless hoti hain: har request mein model sirf wahi dekhta hai jo us request mein bheja gaya. Isliye app har baar zaroori history khud bhejta hai. Option A ka trap chat apps ka experience hai, jahan app hi history dobara bhej raha hota hai. Option B galat hai: normal inference se weights kabhi update nahi hote.

questions.question: Aap invoices se `invoice_number` aur `total` nikaal rahe ho aur chahte ho ki same invoice par baar-baar chalane se output na badle. Temperature ke baare mein sabse sahi choice kya hai?
options: Temperature kam (0 ke paas) rakho; output zyada consistent hoga, par phir bhi validate karna padega
Temperature zyada rakho taaki model zyada 'soch' kar accurate answer de
Temperature kam karne se model ki galtiyaan khatam ho jaati hain, validation ki zaroorat nahi
Temperature sirf response ki length control karta hai
questions.explanation: Kam temperature sampling ko sabse probable tokens ki taraf le jaata hai, isliye extraction jaise tasks mein output stable rehta hai. Par stable ka matlab sahi nahi: model consistently galat bhi ho sakta hai, isliye option C ka 'validation ki zaroorat nahi' trap hai. Option B ulta hai: zyada temperature randomness badhata hai, accuracy nahi. Length max-tokens jaisi setting se control hoti hai, temperature se nahi (option D).

questions.question: Ek (kalpanik) model ki context window 8,000 tokens hai. System prompt 600 tokens ka hai, conversation history 5,900 tokens ki, aur aap answer ke liye 1,000 tokens reserve rakhna chahte ho. Ek retrieved document ke liye zyada se zyada kitne tokens bachte hain?
questions.explanation: Context window mein input aur output dono aate hain: 8,000 − 600 − 5,900 − 1,000 = 500. Option A (1,500) ka trap output ke liye reserve bhool jaana hai; tab model ka jawab beech mein kat sakta hai. Option B (1,100) system prompt ko ginna bhool jaata hai, aur option C sirf system prompt ghataata hai.

questions.question: Sentiment classifier ka prompt hai 'Is review ka sentiment batao.' Model kabhi `Positive`, kabhi `The sentiment is positive.`, kabhi `Label: POSITIVE` deta hai, aur parser toot jaata hai. Sabse effective sudhaar kaunsa hai?
options: Exact output format batana (sirf `positive`/`negative`/`neutral` mein se ek, ya in labels wala JSON), 2-3 examples dena, aur output ko allowed set se validate karna
Temperature badhana taaki model zyada options try kare
Review ko prompt se pehle uppercase mein badal dena
questions.explanation: Problem ambiguous format ki hai, isliye format ko explicit karna (allowed values ya schema), few-shot examples se pattern dikhana aur code mein validate karna seedha ilaaj hai. Option C ulta asar karta hai: zyada temperature output ko aur variable banata hai. Option A tone badalta hai par format ki ambiguity nahi hatata, isliye ye 'kuch to kiya' wala trap hai.

questions.question: Model ne ye JSON lautaya aur aapne use parse kiya. Is Python code ka output kya hoga?
questions.code:
import json
raw = '{"name": "Asha", "age": "29", "skills": ["sql", "git"]}'
d = json.loads(raw)
print(type(d["age"]).__name__, d["age"] * 2, len(d["skills"]))
options: `TypeError`, kyunki string ko int se multiply nahi kar sakte
questions.explanation: JSON mein `"29"` quotes mein hai, isliye `json.loads` use string banata hai, int nahi. Python mein string × int repetition hai: `"29" * 2` = `"2929"`. `skills` list mein 2 items hain. Ye isi baat ka example hai ki schema validation kyun chahiye: model ne age ko string mein de diya. Option A ka trap ye maanna hai ki number jaisa dikhne wala value apne aap int ban jaayega; option C ka trap ye sochna ki string * int error deta hai.

questions.question: 2,000 reviews classify karne hain. Har request mein 250 tokens ke instructions aur ek review (average 100 tokens) jaata hai. Aap batching karte ho: har request mein wahi 250 tokens ke instructions ek baar, aur 20 reviews. Batched version mein kul kitne INPUT tokens lagenge?
questions.explanation: 2,000 ÷ 20 = 100 requests. Har request: 250 + 20 × 100 = 2,250 tokens. Kul: 100 × 2,250 = 225,000. Bina batching ke 2,000 × (250 + 100) = 700,000 hote (option A), yaani bachat sirf instructions ke repeat na hone se hai. Option C ka trap instructions ko bilkul na ginna hai (100 × 2,000), aur option D sirf instructions ginta hai.

weeks.title: Embeddings, Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Evaluating LLM Systems
weeks.summary: Is week aap embeddings aur cosine similarity se semantic search, documents ko chunk karke retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline banana, retrieval aur answers ko evaluate karna, aur hallucination aur prompt injection jaise risks ko kam karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Embedding**: ek model text (ya image) ko fixed length ke numbers ke vector mein badalta hai, aisa ki milte-julte matlab wale texts ke vectors paas-paas hon. 'Refund kab milega?' aur 'paise wapas kitne din mein aate hain?' mein common words kam hain, par embeddings paas honge. Isse keyword search ki jagah meaning-based (semantic) search possible hoti hai.

**Cosine similarity**: do vectors ke beech angle ka cosine: `cos θ = (a·b) / (|a| |b|)`. Value −1 se 1 ke beech; 1 matlab same direction, 0 matlab perpendicular. Ye vector ki length ignore karta hai, sirf direction dekhta hai. Agar vectors pehle se unit length par normalised hain, to cosine similarity seedha dot product ke barabar hoti hai, jo compute karna sasta hai.

**Vector search**: saare document chunks ke embeddings ek baar compute karke store karo. Query aane par uska embedding banao aur sabse zyada similarity wale top-k chunks lao. Lakhon vectors par har ek se compare karna dheema hai, isliye vector indexes approximate nearest-neighbour methods use karte hain jo thodi accuracy ke badle bahut speed dete hain.

**Chunking**: lambe documents ko chhote hisson mein todte hain kyunki (1) poora document context window mein nahi aata, aur (2) chhota focused chunk query se behtar match karta hai. Chunk size aur overlap trade-off hai: bahut chhota chunk context kho deta hai, bahut bada chunk irrelevant text bhar deta hai. Overlap isliye rakhte hain taaki boundary par kati baat kisi ek chunk mein poori mile.

**RAG pipeline**: query → embedding → top-k chunks retrieve → prompt mein chunks + instruction ('sirf diye gaye context se jawab do, source cite karo, na mile to bolo ki pata nahi') → LLM answer. Fayda: model ke training data ke baahar ki ya taaza jaankari bina model retrain kiye use hoti hai; document badla to sirf uska embedding update karo. Answer ki quality retrieval ki quality se zyada nahi ho sakti.

**Evaluation**: 'demo mein achha laga' evaluation nahi hai. Ek golden set banao: questions, unke sahi answers aur relevant documents. Retrieval ke liye recall@k (relevant docs mein se kitne top-k mein aaye) aur precision@k (top-k mein se kitne relevant) nikaalo; answers ke liye correctness, faithfulness (kya answer context se support hota hai) aur format checks. Prompt ya chunking badalne par same set dobara chalao, taaki regression pakda jaaye.

**Hallucination aur safety**: hallucination matlab model ka confident par galat ya bina source wala claim. Kam karne ke tareeke: grounding (RAG), citations maangna, 'pata nahi' bolne ki ijaazat dena, aur output ko facts/rules se check karna. Retrieved documents mein bhi malicious instructions ho sakte hain (indirect prompt injection), aur personal data context mein jaa sakta hai; isliye sources filter karo, permissions limited rakho aur sensitive data mask karo.

example.problem: Ek (kalpanik) company ke help-center ke liye do chunk vectors aur ek query vector diye hain. Cosine similarity nikaal kar batao kaunsa chunk retrieve hoga: query q = (1, 2, 2), chunk A = (2, 0, 1), chunk B = (2, 4, 4).
example.code:
import math

def cosine(a, b):
    dot = sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))
    return dot / (math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a)) * math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b)))

q = [1, 2, 2]
print(round(cosine(q, [2, 0, 1]), 3))   # 0.596
print(round(cosine(q, [2, 4, 4]), 3))   # 1.0
steps: B, q ka hi double hai (same direction), isliye cosine 1; length ka koi asar nahi.
Dot product akela dekhte to bhi B jeet-ta, par lambe vectors ko dot product mein galat fayda mil sakta hai; cosine ye bias hata deta hai.
Answer: **chunk B (cosine 1.0) retrieve hoga**, chunk A ka score ≈ 0.596.

mistakes: Retrieval ko check kiye bina sirf prompt ko tweak karte rehna. Agar sahi chunk top-k mein aaya hi nahi, to koi prompt sahi jawab nahi dila sakta. Fix: pehle recall@k measure karo, phir chunking/embedding/k sudhaaro.

Query aur documents ke liye alag-alag embedding models use karna. Do models ke vectors alag 'spaces' mein hote hain, unki similarity bematlab hai. Fix: index aur query dono ek hi model se embed karo; model badlo to poora index re-embed karo.
Model ke answer ko citation ke bina final maan lena. Fix: answer ke saath source chunk IDs maango aur check karo ki claim un chunks mein sach mein hai.
revision: Embedding = meaning ka vector; paas = similar.
cos θ = a·b / (|a||b|); normalised vectors par cosine = dot product.
Chunk size aur overlap trade-off; overlap boundary ki baat bachata hai.
RAG = retrieve top-k + grounded prompt + citations.
recall@k = mile hue relevant / kul relevant; precision@k = mile hue relevant / k.
Hallucination aur injection ke liye grounding, citations, validation, limited permissions.

questions.question: Vector a = (3, 4) aur vector b = (6, 8) hai. Inki cosine similarity kya hai?
options: 2, kyunki b ki length a ki do guni hai
questions.explanation: b = 2a, yaani dono same direction mein hain, angle 0 hai aur cos 0 = 1. Calculation: a·b = 18 + 32 = 50, |a| = 5, |b| = 10, 50 / 50 = 1. Cosine length ko normalise kar deta hai, isliye option C ka trap ('lamba vector zyada similar') yahan nahi chalta; cosine kabhi 1 se zyada nahi hota. −1 opposite direction ke liye hota.

questions.question: Ek company ki HR policies har mahine update hoti hain aur aap ek assistant chahte ho jo latest policy ke basis par jawab de aur source bataye. Sabse uchit approach kaunsa hai?
options: Har mahine model ko nayi policies par fine-tune karna aur source batana model par chhod dena
Policies ko poora ek baar prompt mein paste karke hamesha wahi prompt use karna
Temperature 0 karke model se policies yaad karne ko kehna
Policies ko chunk karke embeddings ke saath index karna, har query par relevant chunks retrieve karke prompt mein dena, aur answer ke saath chunk ka source dikhana
questions.explanation: RAG mein knowledge index mein rehti hai, model mein nahi: policy badli to sirf us document ke chunks re-embed karo, aur retrieved chunk ka source seedha dikhaya ja sakta hai. Option A tempting hai par fine-tuning mehenga hai, har update par dobara karna padta hai, aur model reliable tarike se source nahi bata paata. Option B context window aur staleness dono problems laata hai. Option C mein model ke paas policy hai hi nahi, to temperature kuch nahi badlega.

questions.question: Query vector q = (1, 2, 2) aur document vector d = (2, 0, 1) hai. Inki cosine similarity (2 decimal tak) kya hai?
questions.explanation: q·d = 1×2 + 2×0 + 2×1 = 4. |q| = √9 = 3, |d| = √5 ≈ 2.236. cosine = 4 / (3 × 2.236) = 4 / 6.708 ≈ 0.596 ≈ 0.60. Option D ka trap sirf dot product (4) likh dena hai, jo normalise nahi hua; cosine 1 se bada ho hi nahi sakta. Option A (0.80) = 4/5 aur option B (0.45) ≈ 4/9 tab aate hain jab sirf ek vector ki squared length (|d|² = 5 ya |q|² = 9) se divide kar diya jaaye, dono norms ke product se nahi.

questions.question: Saare vectors unit length ke hain, isliye score = dot product hai. Is code ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Scores: refund = 0.6×0.8 + 0.8×0.6 = 0.96, shipping = 1.0×0.8 + 0 = 0.8, warranty = 0 + 1.0×0.6 = 0.6. Descending order mein top-2: refund (0.96), shipping (0.8). Option C ka trap q ke components ko ulta (0.6, 0.8) padh lena hai, jisse warranty ka score 0.8 ho jaata. `sorted(scores, ...)` dict ki keys sort karta hai, isliye output naamon ki list hai.

questions.question: 1,000 tokens ka document hai. Is chunking function ka output kya hoga?
questions.explanation: Har agla chunk `size − overlap` = 250 tokens aage shuru hota hai: 0, 250, 500, 750. Start 750 par chunk 750 + 300 = 1050 ≥ 1000 tak pahunchta hai, yaani document ka end cover ho gaya, to loop ruk jaata hai. Option A ka trap overlap ko bhool kar 300 ke step lena hai; option C overlap ko ghatane ki jagah jod deta hai (350). Option B ek khaali chunk 1000 se shuru kar deta, jo loop ki `break` condition hone nahi deti.

questions.question: Golden set mein ek query ke relevant documents {d2, d5, d7} hain. Aapke retriever ne top-5 mein [d5, d1, d9, d2, d4] lautaye. recall@5 aur precision@5 kya hain?
questions.explanation: Top-5 mein relevant documents d5 aur d2 hain, yaani 2 hits. recall@5 = hits / kul relevant = 2/3 ≈ 0.67 (d7 chhoot gaya). precision@5 = hits / k = 2/5 = 0.40. Option A dono formulas ko ulta kar deta hai, jo sabse common trap hai. Option D precision ka denominator k ki jagah relevant docs ki ginti (3) le leta hai.

weeks.title: Sourcing Data from Web APIs and Websites, Responsibly
weeks.summary: Is week aap web APIs se data laana, authentication aur API keys ko sahi jagah rakhna, pagination ke tareeke (offset aur cursor), rate limits aur backoff ke saath retry, aur scraping se pehle `robots.txt`, terms aur privacy ka dhyaan rakhna seekhoge.
concepts: **API pehle, scraping baad mein**: agar data ka official API hai to woh structured (JSON), documented aur stable hota hai, aur provider ki shartein saaf hoti hain. HTML scraping tab jab API na ho; woh page ka design badalte hi toot sakta hai. Dono mein provider ke terms of service padhna aapki zimmedaari hai.

**Authentication**: API key ek secret string hai jo batati hai ki request kaun bhej raha hai; aksar `Authorization: Bearer <token>` ya custom header (jaise `X-API-Key`) mein jaati hai. OAuth mein user kisi app ko limited permission (scope) deta hai aur app ko token milta hai, password nahi. Keys environment variables mein rakho, URL mein nahi, kyunki URLs logs aur history mein save hote hain.

**Offset/page pagination**: `?limit=50&offset=100` ya `?page=3&per_page=50`. Simple hai aur kisi bhi page par jump kar sakte ho, par agar paging ke dauraan data add/delete ho to records shift ho jaate hain: kuch do baar aate hain, kuch chhoot jaate hain. Bahut bade offsets server ke liye mehenge bhi hote hain.

**Cursor pagination**: server har response ke saath ek `next_cursor` (ya `next` URL) deta hai jo 'kahan tak padha' ko encode karta hai, aur aap agli request mein wahi bhejte ho jab tak woh khaali na ho jaaye. Ye ek stable sort key (jaise id ya timestamp) par based hota hai, isliye naye inserts se duplicates/skips nahi hote. Loop ki stopping condition hamesha response se lo (khaali page ya null cursor), apne andaaze se nahi.

**Rate limits**: providers ek time window mein requests ki limit lagaate hain. Limit cross hone par 429 Too Many Requests aata hai, aksar `Retry-After` header ke saath. Sahi reaction: utna wait karo, phir exponential backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, ...) ek maximum cap aur thode random jitter ke saath, aur ek max retry count. 5xx par bhi backoff se retry theek hai; 400/401/403/404 par wahi request dobara bhejna bekaar hai.

**Polite collection**: responses ko cache karo taaki same data baar-baar na maango, requests ke beech delay rakho, apna User-Agent pehchaan-yogya rakho, aur sirf woh fields lo jo chahiye. Raw responses ko disk par save karna (timestamp ke saath) reproducibility aur debugging dono mein madad karta hai.

**robots.txt aur ethics**: website ke root par `/robots.txt` crawlers ke liye rules deta hai: `User-agent` (kis bot ke liye), `Disallow: /path` (is prefix se shuru hone wale URLs mat lo), `Allow: /path` (exception). Matching path PREFIX par hoti hai, isliye `Disallow: /search` `/searchable` ko bhi rokta hai. Ye technically voluntary hai, par ise maanna professional standard hai. Personal data, login ke peeche ka content aur copyright wala material legal aur ethical sawal uthate hain, sirf technical nahi.

example.problem: Ek (kalpanik) API `GET /v1/orders?cursor=...` har page par max 100 orders aur `next_cursor` deta hai, aur kabhi-kabhi 429 lautata hai. Saare orders laane wala robust loop likho.
steps: Token environment variable se aata hai aur `Authorization` header mein jaata hai, URL mein nahi.
Har request par `timeout` diya hai, taaki atki hui connection program ko hamesha ke liye na rok de.
429 ya 5xx par `Retry-After` ho to utna, warna 1, 2, 4, 8, ... second (60 par cap) wait, plus thoda random jitter taaki kai clients ek saath retry na karein.
4xx (429 ke alawa) par `raise_for_status()` turant error deta hai, kyunki dobara bhejne se kuch nahi badlega.
Cursor loop tab tak chalta hai jab tak server `next_cursor` deta hai; stopping condition server se aati hai.
Answer: **cursor-based loop + header auth + timeout + capped exponential backoff with jitter** saare orders bina duplicate ke laata hai.

mistakes: 429 milne par turant tight loop mein retry karna. Isse limit aur der tak lagi rehti hai aur key block ho sakti hai. Fix: `Retry-After` maano, warna exponential backoff with cap aur jitter.

Pagination loop ko 'jab tak page number 10 tak na pahunche' jaisi fixed condition par chalana. Data kam-zyada hote hi records chhootenge ya khaali calls hongi. Fix: server ke signal (khaali page, `next` null, ya total count) se ruko.

Ye maan lena ki jo page browser mein public dikhta hai use bina soche bulk mein scrape karna theek hai. Terms, `robots.txt`, server load aur personal data ka dhyaan rakhna zaroori hai. Fix: pehle API dhoondho, rules padho, rate limit lagao, aur sirf zaroori data lo.
revision: API key header mein, environment se; URL mein kabhi nahi.
Offset pagination simple par changing data par duplicates/skips; cursor stable.
429 = rate limit; `Retry-After`, phir capped exponential backoff + jitter.
400/401/403/404 ko retry mat karo; 429/5xx ko backoff se.
`robots.txt`: `Disallow`/`Allow` path prefix match karte hain.
Cache, delay, clear User-Agent, minimum data: polite collection.

questions.question: Ek data collection script ko API se `429 Too Many Requests` response aur header `Retry-After: 30` milta hai. Sabse sahi reaction kya hai?
options: Turant same request dobara bhejna, jab tak 200 na mil jaaye
Rate limit cross hui hai; kam se kam 30 second ruk kar retry karna, aur aage bhi backoff ke saath requests dheemi karna
API key galat hai; nayi key generate karna
Server crash ho gaya hai; usi waqt doosre endpoint par switch karna
questions.explanation: 429 ka matlab hai client ne allowed rate se zyada requests bheji hain, aur `Retry-After` batata hai kitni der rukna hai. Isliye wait karke retry karna aur rate kam karna sahi hai. Option A sabse common galti hai: tight-loop retry limit ko aur lamba kheenchta hai aur key block karwa sakta hai. Galat key par 401/403 aata, aur server crash 5xx hota, isliye options C aur D galat hain.

questions.question: Ek notebook ek paid API ko call karta hai aur repo team ke saath share hota hai. API key ko kaise use karna sabse sahi hai?
options: Key environment variable (ya gitignored `.env`) se padho aur request header mein bhejo
Key ko URL query mein `?api_key=...` ki tarah bhejo, kyunki HTTPS sab encrypt kar deta hai
Key notebook ke pehle cell mein likh do; private repo hai to koi dikkat nahi
Key ko base64 mein encode karke code mein rakho, taaki koi padh na sake
questions.explanation: Environment se padhne par key code aur git history se bahar rehti hai, aur header mein bhejne par woh URL logs mein nahi aati. Option B ka trap ye hai ki HTTPS network par to encrypt karta hai, par URL server access logs, proxies aur browser history mein phir bhi record hota hai. Option C mein key history mein hamesha ke liye reh jaati hai aur repo kabhi bhi public ya fork ho sakta hai. Base64 encryption nahi, sirf encoding hai, koi bhi decode kar sakta hai (option D).

questions.question: Ek API mein 237 records hain aur woh `?limit=50&offset=...` pagination deta hai (offset 0 se shuru). Aapka loop tab rukta hai jab kisi page par 50 se kam records aayein. Kitni requests hongi aur aakhri request kya laayegi?
questions.explanation: Offsets 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 = 5 requests. Pehli chaar mein 50-50 = 200 records, aakhri (offset 200) mein 237 − 200 = 37 records, jo 50 se kam hain, to loop ruk jaata hai. Option B ka trap offset ko page number × 50 maan kar 1 se shuru karna hai (50, 100, ..., 250). Option C tab sahi hota jab total 50 ka multiple hota (jaise 250), tab ek khaali page dekhkar hi rukna padta.

questions.question: Retry policy: pehla wait 1 second, har retry par double, par koi bhi wait 10 second se zyada nahi, aur kul 5 retries. Ye code kya print karega (jitter ignore karo)?
questions.code:
waits = [min(10, 1 * 2**i) for i in range(5)]
print(waits, sum(waits))
questions.explanation: `i` 0 se 4 tak: 2⁰..2⁴ = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. Cap `min(10, ...)` aakhri 16 ko 10 kar deta hai: [1, 2, 4, 8, 10], sum 25. Option A ka trap cap ko bhool jaana hai. Option B `range(5)` ko 4 values samajh leta hai. Option D `min` ko `max` ki tarah padhta hai.

questions.question: Ek site ka `robots.txt` neeche hai. Aapka crawler (koi bhi user agent) inmein se kaunsa path fetch kar sakta hai?
questions.code:
User-agent: *
Allow: /private/press/
Disallow: /private/
Disallow: /search
questions.explanation: `/private/press/note.html` `Allow: /private/press/` se match karta hai, jo `Disallow: /private/` ka zyada specific exception hai, isliye allowed. `/private/reports/q1.csv` sirf `Disallow: /private/` se match hota hai. Rules path PREFIX par lagte hain: `Disallow: /search` `/search?q=tools` ko bhi rokta hai aur `/searchable-items` ko bhi, kyunki dono `/search` se shuru hote hain. Option B sabse tempting trap hai, kyunki log ise poore word ka match samajhte hain.

questions.question: Ek API posts ko newest-first order mein `?limit=50&offset=...` se deta hai. Aapne page 1 (offset 0) liya. Page 2 (offset 50) maangne se pehle site par 3 nayi posts publish ho gayi. Page 2 mein kya hoga?
options: Page 2 bilkul sahi rahega, kyunki offset fix hai
Page 1 ki aakhri 3 posts page 2 mein dobara aayengi (duplicates), aur koi post skip nahi hogi
3 posts skip ho jaayengi aur kabhi nahi milengi
Nayi 3 posts page 2 ke shuru mein aa jaayengi
questions.explanation: 3 nayi posts list ke top par judti hain, to purani har post ki position 3 badh jaati hai. Page 1 ne purani positions 0–49 di thi. Ab offset 50 par jo posts hain woh purani positions 47–96 hain, to purani 47, 48, 49 (page 1 ki aakhri teen) dobara aati hain. Option C ka trap ulta case hai: skip tab hota jab paging ke dauraan posts DELETE hoti. Nayi posts offset 0–2 par hain, page 2 mein nahi (option D). Isi wajah se changing data par cursor pagination behtar hai.

weeks.title: Parsing Formats, Querying Databases and Extracting with Regular Expressions
weeks.summary: Is week aap HTML ko CSS selectors se, nested JSON ko safely, aur CSV ko sahi parser se padhna, PDF se nikle text ki dikkatein samajhna, databases ko parameterised SQL se source ki tarah use karna, aur regular expressions se patterns extract karna seekhoge.
concepts: **HTML aur CSS selectors**: HTML ek tree (DOM) hai: elements, unke attributes (`id`, `class`, `href`) aur text. Parser (jaise BeautifulSoup ya lxml) is tree mein selectors se elements dhoondhta hai: `td` (tag), `.price` (class), `#items` (id), `#items .price` (items ke andar kahin bhi price, descendant), `tr > td` (direct child), `a[href]` (jismein href attribute ho). Text `get_text()` se aur link `['href']` se nikalte hain; relative links ko base URL ke saath `urljoin` se poora karo.

**Nested JSON**: API responses aksar nested hote hain: list ke andar dicts, dicts ke andar lists. Har field har record mein ho, ye maan kar `item["tags"]` likhoge to ek missing field poora job gira degi; `item.get("tags", [])` jaisa default do. Analysis ke liye nested data ko flat table (ek row per record, ya ek row per record-tag pair) mein badalna padta hai, aur ye decide karna padta hai ki list wale fields ka kya karna hai.

**CSV ke jaal**: CSV mein field ke andar comma ho to field double quotes mein hota hai (`"Mumbai, MH"`), quotes ke andar quote double ho jaata hai (`""`), aur ek field mein newline bhi ho sakti hai. Isliye `line.split(",")` galat hai; Python ka `csv` module ya pandas ka reader use karo. Encoding (UTF-8, UTF-8 with BOM, purani files mein kuch aur), delimiter (`;` ya tab) aur header row hamesha check karo.

**PDF se nikla text**: PDF page par characters ki positions store karta hai, 'paragraph' ya 'table' ka structure nahi. Text extraction ke baad aksar milta hai: columns aapas mein mile hue, har page par repeat hone wale header/footer, line ke end par hyphen se tute words, aur tables jo spaces mein bikhar gaye. Scanned PDF mein text hota hi nahi, OCR chahiye. Har extraction ko kuch pages par manually verify karo.

**Database as a source**: production data aksar SQL database mein hota hai. Filtering aur aggregation database mein karo (`WHERE`, `GROUP BY`), poori table download karke Python mein nahi; network aur memory dono bachte hain. Read-only credentials use karo. Query mein user input kabhi string formatting se mat jodo; parameterised query (`?` ya `%s` placeholders) use karo, warna SQL injection se query ka matlab hi badal sakta hai.

**Regular expressions ki basics**: `\d` digit, `\w` word character, `\s` whitespace, `.` (newline ke alawa) koi bhi character, `[A-Z]` character class, quantifiers `*` (0+), `+` (1+), `?` (0/1), `{4}` (exactly 4), anchors `^`/`$`, aur `( )` capture group. Python mein pattern hamesha raw string `r"..."` mein likho taaki backslash Python khud na kha jaaye.

**Greedy vs lazy aur findall**: `.*` greedy hai, jitna ho sake utna match karta hai; `.*?` lazy hai, kam se kam. `re.findall` agar pattern mein koi group nahi to poore matches ki list, ek group ho to us group ke strings ki list, aur do ya zyada groups hon to tuples ki list deta hai. Ye rule bhoolna extraction code mein sabse common bug hai.

example.problem: Ek (kalpanik) supplier ke invoice ka PDF-extracted text hai. Usse invoice number aur saari dates (DD/MM/YYYY) nikaal kar ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD) mein badlo.
example.code:
import re

text = """ACME Supplies Pvt Ltd (fictional)    Page 1 of 2
Invoice No: INV-2024-0173
Issue date: 05/03/2024   Due date: 04/04/2024
Payment re-
ceived on 28/03/2024"""

weeks.title: Data Preparation: Cleaning, Tidy Data, Joins and Command-Line Tools
weeks.summary: Is week aap missing values, galat types, duplicates aur outliers ko soch-samajh kar handle karna, data ko tidy shape mein laana, joins aur reshaping ke row-count effects samajhna, aur `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `sort`, `uniq`, `jq` jaise command-line tools se tez cleaning karna seekhoge.
concepts: **Missing values pehchaano**: missing hamesha `NaN`/`None` ki shakal mein nahi aata; khaali string, `"NA"`, `"-"`, `-999` ya `0` jaise sentinel values bhi ho sakte hain. Pehle saare variants ko ek standard missing marker mein badlo, phir har column mein missing ka count aur pattern dekho: kya ye random hai ya kisi khaas group (jaise ek city ya ek date range) mein zyada hai? Pattern se hi decide hota hai ki kya karna hai.

**Missing handle karne ke options**: rows drop karna (missing kam aur random ho to theek, warna bias), impute karna (numeric mein median aksar mean se safe, categorical mein mode ya 'Unknown'), ya ek indicator column (`income_missing = 1`) banana. Mean imputation se column ka mean nahi badalta par variance kam ho jaata hai aur correlations kamzor dikhte hain, isliye imputed values ko 'asli' data mat samjho aur kya kiya woh document karo.

**Types aur formats**: numbers jo text ki tarah aaye (`"1,200"`, `"₹950"`, `"12 %"`), dates jo alag formats mein hon (`05/03/2024` DD/MM hai ya MM/DD?), aur categories jinki spelling alag ho (`Delhi`, `delhi `, `New Delhi`). Cleaning ka matlab: whitespace strip, case normalise, symbols aur thousand separators hatao, explicit format ke saath date parse karo, aur conversion fail hone wali values ko gin kar dekho, chupchaap drop mat karo.

**Duplicates aur outliers**: exact duplicate rows aasaani se pakdi jaati hain, par asli sawal 'business key' ka hai: kya same `order_id` do baar aaya? Outlier detection ke liye IQR rule (Q1 − 1.5·IQR se neeche ya Q3 + 1.5·IQR se upar) ya z-score use karte hain, par flag karna aur delete karna alag cheezein hain: pehle dekho ki value data entry error hai (age 420) ya genuinely rare event (ek bada order).

**Tidy data**: har variable ek column, har observation ek row, har type ki observational unit ek table. Wide table (`city, 2022, 2023, 2024`) mein saal column headers mein chhupa hai; use long format (`city, year, sales`) mein badalna 'melt'/'unpivot' kehlata hai, aur ulta 'pivot'. Long format grouping, plotting aur joins ke liye aasaan hota hai; wide format insaan ke padhne ke liye.

**Joins aur row counts**: inner join sirf matching keys rakhta hai, left join left table ki har row rakhta hai (match na mile to NULLs), full outer dono taraf ki. Agar right table mein ek key do baar hai, to us key ki har left row do baar aayegi: join ke baad row count badh jaata hai. Isliye join se pehle key ki uniqueness check karo aur join ke baad row count compare karo; yeh sabse common silent bug hai.

**Command-line tools**: `grep pattern` matching lines, `cut -d, -f2` column, `sort | uniq -c` frequency count, `sed 's/old/new/g'` text replace, `awk -F, '{s[$1]+=$2}'` group-wise sum, aur `jq '.items[].id'` JSON se fields. Bade log/CSV files par ye bina poori file memory mein load kiye stream karte hain aur pipeline mein jud jaate hain. Simple CSV ke liye theek, par quoted commas wale CSV par `cut`/`awk -F,` toot sakte hain; tab ek proper CSV parser use karo.

example.problem: Ek (kalpanik) store ki `sales.csv` mein header `city,amount` hai. Har city ka total amount nikaalo aur sabse zyada wali city batao, sirf command line se.
example.code:
printf 'city,amount
Pune,10
Delhi,5
Pune,7
Mumbai,3
Delhi,8
' > sales.csv

awk -F, 'NR > 1 { total[$1] += $2 }
         END { for (c in total) print c, total[c] }' sales.csv \
  | sort -k2,2nr \
  | head -1
steps: `-F,` awk ko batata hai ki fields comma se alag hain; `$1` city aur `$2` amount hai.
`NR > 1` header row (record number 1) ko skip karta hai, warna 'city' bhi ek group ban jaata.
`total[$1] += $2` associative array mein har city ka running sum rakhta hai: Pune 10 + 7 = 17, Delhi 5 + 8 = 13, Mumbai 3.
`END` block saari lines ke baad chalta hai aur har city ka total print karta hai (order guaranteed nahi).
`sort -k2,2nr` doosre field ko number ki tarah descending sort karta hai, isliye order ki guarantee na hone se fark nahi padta.
Answer: **`Pune 17`** (`head -1` sirf top line rakhta hai).

mistakes: Join ke baad row count check na karna. Lookup table mein duplicate key ho to facts table ki rows chupchaap double ho jaati hain aur totals galat aate hain. Fix: join se pehle key ki uniqueness assert karo aur baad mein counts compare karo.

Missing ko 0 se bhar dena. Isse mean aur totals neeche khisak jaate hain aur 'no data' ka matlab 'zero sales' ban jaata hai. Fix: missing ko missing rehne do, ya soch-samajh kar median/indicator use karo aur document karo.
Har outlier ko automatically delete kar dena. Kai baar wahi asli signal hota hai (fraud, bada customer). Fix: pehle flag karo, kuch cases khud dekho, phir rule ke saath decide karo.
revision: Missing ke saare roop (`""`, `NA`, `-999`) pehle ek standard marker mein.
Mean imputation: mean same, variance kam.
Tidy: variable = column, observation = row; wide → long = melt.
Right table mein duplicate keys = join ke baad zyada rows.
IQR fences: Q1 − 1.5·IQR aur Q3 + 1.5·IQR; flag ≠ delete.
`awk`, `sort`, `uniq -c`, `cut`, `sed`, `jq`: tez streaming cleaning.

Option C ka trap fences ko 1.5 × IQR ki jagah sirf IQR (10 aur 40) se banana hai, jisse 8 bhi flag ho jaata. Option A ka trap sirf bade outliers dhoondhna hai; IQR rule dono taraf check karta hai.
